In SCOPe 2.04 the two domains were in different folds. ColG's collagen-binding domain (1nqd chain B, d1nqdb_, SUNID 86026) was in b.23.2.1, the Collagen-binding domain family and superfamily (b.23.2) in the CUB-like fold (b.23). The Cry3A (CRYIIIA, Bacillus thuringiensis tenebrionis) C-terminal domain (1dlc A:500-644, d1dlca1, SUNID 23719) was in b.18.1.3, delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain, in the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily (b.18.1) and fold (b.18). Both were class b, but in 2.04 SCOPe did not infer common ancestry between them. They were in different superfamilies and folds.

In current SCOPe (2.08) the ColG domain (1nqd B:893-1008, d1nqdb1, same SUNID 86026) is in b.18.1.36, Collagen-binding domain, protein 'Class 1 collagenase', species Clostridium histolyticum. It sits in the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily b.18.1 (SUNID 49785) and fold b.18. This is the same superfamily as d1dlca1 (b.18.1.3, delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain, family SUNID 49796). So the relationship changed from 'different folds, no inferred homology' to 'same fold and same superfamily'. The two remain in different families (b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3), so they are classed as remote homologs, not close family relatives. The old b.23.2 collagen-binding superfamily was folded into b.18.1 as a new family, and the CUB-like placement was abandoned. The 2.08 record also splits 1nqd chain B into the domain b1 (893-1008) and a short linker segment b2 (891-892, l.1.1.1), and chain A (d1nqda_) is also b.18.1.36. The 2.08 domain definitions are more precise than the whole-chain 2.04 entries.

In SCOPe, being in the same superfamily means common ancestry is inferred. The tool output shows homology_implied_by_level=true for both domains at the superfamily level. The superfamily assignment is the supporting evidence for this. The following supporting evidence comes from outside the SCOPe records I retrieved and from my own knowledge, so I have not checked it here. (1) Structural: both are beta-sandwich jelly-roll domains with the galactose-binding-domain (discoidin/F5/8 type C-like) topology. The ColG collagen-binding domain (CBD) is a beta-sandwich of about 110 residues with bound Ca2+, and Cry3A domain III is a jelly-roll beta-sandwich. Superposition shows a shared core of strands and similar topology, which is what a structure-based remote-homology call requires. Structure similarity alone (fold) is not proof of homology, but here the detailed topology, a shared ligand-binding/carbohydrate-binding-like role in a bacterial secreted protein, and the SCOPe curators' reassignment together justify superfamily-level merging. (2) Functional: both are accessory binding domains of secreted bacterial proteins, one binding collagen (ColG) and one binding receptors or carbohydrates for the toxin (Cry3A domain III, which has been implicated in receptor binding and specificity). This is a shared general role as a binding module in a beta-sandwich, consistent with divergence from a common carbohydrate/ligand-binding ancestor. The binding specificities differ (collagen for ColG, insect-gut receptors for Cry3A), and the domains share little sequence identity. (3) Contextual: fold b.18 members are mostly ligand-binding modules, which supports a plausible ancestral binding function.

Limits: the change is a classification revision driven by new structural evidence, and it implies homology only at the superfamily level. It does not show close sequence similarity, shared binding specificity, or shared mechanism. Function should not be transferred between the two: ColG's collagen binding does not predict Cry3A's receptor interaction, and vice versa. The two domains also sit in different multidomain contexts (ColG is a metalloprotease with a catalytic domain, Cry3A is a three-domain pore-forming toxin whose other domains are b.77.2.1 and f.1.3.1). Domain classification applies only to the reference domains named, and the other 1dlc domains (d1dlca2 b.77.2.1 and d1dlca3 f.1.3.1) are unrelated to ColG's CBD. I did not retrieve alignments, RMSD values, or the primary-literature basis, so the specifics of the structural evidence are from background knowledge.

In SCOPe 2.04 the two domains were in different folds. ColG's collagen-binding domain (1nqd chain B, d1nqdb_, SUNID 86026) was in b.23.2.1, the Collagen-binding domain family and superfamily (b.23.2) in the CUB-like fold (b.23). The Cry3A (CRYIIIA, Bacillus thuringiensis tenebrionis) C-terminal domain (1dlc A:500-644, d1dlca1, SUNID 23719) was in b.18.1.3, delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain, in the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily (b.18.1) and fold (b.18). Both were class b, but in 2.04 SCOPe did not infer common ancestry between them. They were in different superfamilies and folds.

In current SCOPe (2.08) the ColG domain (1nqd B:893-1008, d1nqdb1, same SUNID 86026) is in b.18.1.36, Collagen-binding domain, protein 'Class 1 collagenase', species Clostridium histolyticum. It sits in the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily b.18.1 (SUNID 49785) and fold b.18. This is the same superfamily as d1dlca1 (b.18.1.3, delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain, family SUNID 49796). So the relationship changed from 'different folds, no inferred homology' to 'same fold and same superfamily'. The two remain in different families (b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3), so they are classed as remote homologs, not close family relatives. The old b.23.2 collagen-binding superfamily was folded into b.18.1 as a new family, and the CUB-like placement was abandoned. The 2.08 record also splits 1nqd chain B into the domain b1 (893-1008) and a short linker segment b2 (891-892, l.1.1.1), and chain A (d1nqda_) is also b.18.1.36. The 2.08 domain definitions are more precise than the whole-chain 2.04 entries.

In SCOPe, being in the same superfamily means common ancestry is inferred. The tool output shows homology_implied_by_level=true for both domains at the superfamily level. The superfamily assignment is the supporting evidence for this. The following supporting evidence comes from outside the SCOPe records I retrieved and from my own knowledge, so I have not checked it here. (1) Structural: both are beta-sandwich jelly-roll domains with the galactose-binding-domain (discoidin/F5/8 type C-like) topology. The ColG collagen-binding domain (CBD) is a beta-sandwich of about 110 residues with bound Ca2+, and Cry3A domain III is a jelly-roll beta-sandwich. Superposition shows a shared core of strands and similar topology, which is what a structure-based remote-homology call requires. Structure similarity alone (fold) is not proof of homology, but here the detailed topology, a shared ligand-binding/carbohydrate-binding-like role in a bacterial secreted protein, and the SCOPe curators' reassignment together justify superfamily-level merging. (2) Functional: both are accessory binding domains of secreted bacterial proteins, one binding collagen (ColG) and one binding receptors or carbohydrates for the toxin (Cry3A domain III, which has been implicated in receptor binding and specificity). This is a shared general role as a binding module in a beta-sandwich, consistent with divergence from a common carbohydrate/ligand-binding ancestor. The binding specificities differ (collagen for ColG, insect-gut receptors for Cry3A), and the domains share little sequence identity. (3) Contextual: fold b.18 members are mostly ligand-binding modules, which supports a plausible ancestral binding function.

Limits: the change is a classification revision driven by new structural evidence, and it implies homology only at the superfamily level. It does not show close sequence similarity, shared binding specificity, or shared mechanism. Function should not be transferred between the two: ColG's collagen binding does not predict Cry3A's receptor interaction, and vice versa. The two domains also sit in different multidomain contexts (ColG is a metalloprotease with a catalytic domain, Cry3A is a three-domain pore-forming toxin whose other domains are b.77.2.1 and f.1.3.1). Domain classification applies only to the reference domains named, and the other 1dlc domains (d1dlca2 b.77.2.1 and d1dlca3 f.1.3.1) are unrelated to ColG's CBD. I did not retrieve alignments, RMSD values, or the primary-literature basis, so the specifics of the structural evidence are from background knowledge.
